full_judgment:
6. The plaintiff is the owner in possession of the building and other structures standing on 0.29 acre of the land in CS Plot Nos. 2203 and 2210 under Khatian Nos. 218 and 298 of Mouza Chuadanga in Chuadanga town in the District of Kushtia. The plaintiff acquired the property and obtained possession over it firstly on the basis of a Bainapatra dated 18-12-1963 and subsequently, by Kabala dated 16-1-1964 from the owner Md Mahbub Hossain, the lawful owner in possession, who had acquired the same by exchange from the heirs of CS recorded tenant Upendra Nath Acharjee. In such position, defendant No. 2, the Extra-Assistant Commissioner issued an order of requisition of the suit property dated 25-5-1964 for providing accommodation to the branch office of the National Bank of Pakistan in the Town of Chuadanga District, addressing the plaintiff's husband, who was an officer of the then Government of East Pakistan, and had been working as a Circle Officer in different outlying areas of the country. In 1964, the plaintiff's husband was serving at Kishoregonj Sub-Division. Though the Bank had its existing office in a proper place in the town, yet requisition and acquisition was done with ulterior motive without serving any notice to the plaintiff. No sooner had the plaintiff come to know the matter, than he raised objection to defendant No. 2, and preferred an appeal to the Commissioner, lamina Division, and thereafter, to the Government through the Secretary, Revenue Department on 26-12-1964, but, they did not give any reply. After that, the plaintiff filed an application on 1-1-1966 to the Minister-in-Charge of Revenue where the plaintiff's application for vacating the order of requisition was rejected, and she was intimated through a letter dated 23-9-1965. Lastly, the plaintiff's prayer for review was also rejected by a letter dated 12-11-1965. After that, the plaintiff had submitted her original unregistered 'Bainapatra' in support of her transaction following the subsequent possession from its lawful owner and title holder of the suit property by exchange within the knowledge of defendant Nos. 1-3. But no notice was ever served on either of them under the provisions of East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of property Act, while the plaintiff was thrown out of her own property most arbitrarily. The Order of permanent acquisition dated 8-6-1966 was disclosed for the first time on 7-11-1970, and the defendant in their written statement in Title Suit No. 51 of 1970 admitted the same, and following the requisition order, defendant No. I forcibly took possession of the suit property on 21-11-1965 after evicting the plaintiff, and in that aspect, the cause of action in Title Suit No. finally arose on 12-11-1965, when the defendants refused to interfere with requisition order made by defendant No.3's Head Office at Dhaka, and also filed Title Suit No. 

 "Once the property is acquired and gazette notification is published under section 5(7) of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (Act XIII of 1948), the right, title and interest if any of the owners are extinguished and preparation of Khatian or payment of rent does not improve the position of the original owners in respect of acquired land."
